quotes.text: That Sabbath morning, my young friend James was wearing a new suit. As the program began, James was examining some of the more interesting aspects of his new suit. What most captured his attention were two features of his jacket. On his jacket sleeves there were buttons but no holes. And on the left lapel of his jacket there was a buttonhole but no buttons. Neither the buttons nor the buttonhole seemed to be serving any real purpose.
quotes.speaker: Elder PaulÂ H. Sinclair
quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Well, James cleverly devised a purpose for both. I anxiously watched as James delightedly buttoned his right sleeve to his left jacket lapel. Being pleased with himself quickly gave way to being panicked, because once James had buttoned his arm to his chest, even with the flexibility of a Primary child, he could not get himself loose. James had unintentionally, but quite successfully, created a one-arm straitjacket.

quotes.talk: Quick to Help, Slow to Judge
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: As James became more and more stuck, I became more and more aggravated. Baffling buttons had been put to an uncomfortable and, to me, irritating purpose. I was shaking my head in disappointment as James was about to go to the pulpit.

quotes.text: Just then I noticed the little girl sitting next to James. She had also witnessed Jamesâs predicament and his growing concern. But instead of being aggravated, she wanted to help. Quickly discerning what action was needed, she reached up with her tiny, nonjudgmental fingers and popped the button out of the buttonhole. James was rescued, and the Primary program was saved!

quotes.text: I felt relieved but also humbled. I recognized the quiet rebuke of a misplaced button and tiny fingers reminding me that I should be trying to be more like Jesus. That small but majestic moment helped me embrace what Elder Patrick Kearon has described as âa radical reorientationâ of my soul. I donât recall the topic of the Primary program that day, but the message I received through the Holy Ghost prompted a spiritual realignment. A little child led me to learn this: that a true disciple of Jesus Christ is quick to help and slow to judge.

quotes.text: The Savior taught this loving principle of discipleship from the very beginning of His mortal ministry. In the Gospel of John, He ministers to a Samaritan woman. We do not know her name. We have come to know her as âthe woman at the well.â Her interaction with the Lord Jesus Christ teaches many lessons. One critical lesson is the example of the Savior being quick to offer grace and transformative help.

quotes.text: As the conversation opened, Jesus was weary and unexpectedly asked the woman for a drink. quotes.text: This woman may have done more to warrant judgment than merely buttoning her sleeve to her lapel. Apparently, she had a series of broken relationships and was, at that moment, living with a man who was not her husband. But what do we actually know about her circumstances? Was she widowed? divorced? abandoned? We do not know. Now, please donât misunderstand me. Her story is very important, but these are not the judgmental details we need to know about her journey.
